lane: independent source-only peer; zero product authorship and zero runtime permit
review_scope: Candidate patch and manifest against current dispatcher, CDP client, Network tab, saved replay callers, approval host, and tests
No patch application, browser exercise, typecheck, or test execution

findings.title: The document-start path still broadcasts each full response into page script listeners
findings.evidence: Candidate network-tap.ts post() calls the CDP binding, then unconditionally calls window.postMessage({__matrx_net:true,event}, window.location.origin). The event includes unredacted URL and response body before document-network-capture.ts applies its whitelist; any same-window message listener can receive it.
findings.impact: The new privileged capture leaks its response body and credential-bearing URL through the old page-message route even when no isolated relay is required for saved replay. Whitelisting only the subsequent CDP event does not close that route.
findings.repair: For binding-backed saved capture, send only through the binding. Preserve window.postMessage solely for the manual Network-tab relay, with a test that listens for message events and asserts absence of a credential canary during saved replay.

findings.title: Approval identity allows a different SPA route in the same document
findings.evidence: Candidate data-patterns.ts prepare() hashes pattern fields, tab id, and chrome.scripting documentId, but not tab.url or the current route. fetchPatternsForDomain selects by host. A same-document history.pushState transition keeps documentId and host, so both pre- and post-approval snapshots can compare equal. The later run() reads its new tab URL as its starting page.
findings.impact: A privileged approval requested on one page can authorize a reload and capture on another same-host SPA page without renewed consent; the result can be attributed to the wrong saved route.
findings.repair: Bind the canonical current page URL or resolved saved route to the approved operation and recheck immediately before Page.reload, with a same-document route-change test through the actual dispatcher.

findings.title: A sidepanel restart can strand a local approval without a visible card
findings.evidence: Candidate SavedReplayApprovalHost.tsx initializes requests to [] and subscribes only to future TOOL_CONFIRM_REQUEST broadcasts. It never loads pending confirms on mount. Candidate dispatch.ts persists before broadcasting, but the local recovery path discards a persisted local approval if a response arrives after SW restart.
findings.impact: If the sidepanel remounts during the five-minute approval window, the request can remain pending in the worker while the user has no card to answer. A restarted worker also cannot finish that local operation, so the UI needs an explicit cancellation/error path.
findings.repair: On host mount reconcile pending local requests or cancel them and surface a terminal error to the waiting run; prove both sidepanel and worker restart cases without a hanging promise.

findings.title: Capture window begins before debugger setup and reload
findings.evidence: Candidate run-interactive.ts creates windowTimer before openDocumentNetworkCapture resolves. Candidate transport starts its own timeout before acquireSession, Page.enable, Runtime.enable, addBinding, script registration, and Page.reload. The existing default is a 20-second window.
findings.impact: Slow debugger attachment or script registration consumes the response capture window and can produce a false no-match immediately after the document starts.
findings.repair: Start the matching window from confirmed arming/reload while retaining a separate bounded setup timeout. Test delayed CDP setup followed by an immediate new-document response.

findings.title: Proposed tests do not prove the complete privacy or saved UI result
findings.evidence: document-network-capture.test.ts asserts request_headers is absent from an emitted event but does not observe window.postMessage. document-network-dispatch.test.ts mocks runSavedPattern, so a green dispatcher test cannot establish that CDP installs before reload or that the saved result reaches PatternsTab/DataView. document-network-recovery.test.ts constructs its own identity directly from the persisted record and returns a stubbed row. No executed red-to-green or constant-return mutation evidence accompanies the scratch candidate.
findings.impact: The suite could pass with the page leak and with broken end-to-end capture or UI delivery.
findings.repair: Add a forcing boundary test for no page message, an actual saved-run UI path with CDP as the sole browser double, and a recovery test whose second prepare reads changed live recipe/document data. Demonstrate red on each targeted break.

positive_findings: CDP addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument is awaited before Page.reload, addressing the known initial-request race in principle.
Runtime event handling rejects old and non-main-frame contexts and buffers early events until the new main frame commits.
Local port sends saved identity rather than caller-supplied approval/config, and the prepared operation requests privileged confirmation even in Act mode.
Candidate cleanup attempts to remove the document script and binding and release the debugger lease.
limitations: All findings are source-derived; no live product or test result is claimed.
The adjacent D48 credential repair was still pending in the shared checkout; its final privacy behavior is not credited to D47.
No claim of runtime or TypeScript correctness is possible from this scratch candidate.
